lisa-peopleops: FYI — new hire Javier M (SWE) tentative start Jun 1. He says EAD expires 2026-05-12 and renewal is pending. Need to confirm onboarding plan (I-9, payroll, benefits). cc @omar-immigration @sam-eng

omar-immigration: Thanks — do we have the USCIS receipt/receipt number? If he filed for renewal (C(9)/C(17) etc.) we need the receipt to document automatic extension. There could be an EAD gap if adjudication is slow.

javier-newhire: I have the receipt notice: RX123456789. Filed 2026-04-10. My attorney says typical 4-6 months. I can be available for ramping but understand I can’t do paid work until I-9/work auth is current, right?

maria-peopleops: :eyes: Quick Q — can he do unpaid onboarding/knowledge transfer sessions before EAD? Or would that create compliance issues?

omar-immigration: Correct — he cannot do productive, paid work without valid work authorization. Limited unpaid shadowing (e.g., <5 hours, purely observational) may be OK in some cases but we should avoid any task that would be considered work. I will check with legal on the exact wording. Please ask Javier to upload the receipt + latest I-94 to the secure onboarding folder.

lisa-peopleops: Hiring manager @sam-eng would like earlier ramp. Any avenue to start as a contractor in the interim (through his attorney) so we can avoid a delayed start? Thoughts on payroll/benefits impact?

hr-bot: Reminder: benefits enrollment is triggered by the employee's first paid day. See internal guide: https://redwoodinference.internal/hr/benefits-enrollment (access required).

omar-immigration: Contractor route has risks (misclassification, procurement, contracting with a foreign entity). Payroll cannot process pay without SSN/EAD. For benefits, we can enroll effective on the first paid date; if we set a placeholder start earlier, benefits admin will need a manual override. I'll loop legal and compensation.

sam-eng: If we must wait for EAD, better to set a realistic start date. Can we target Jun 22 as a fallback? That gives time for the adjudication window and avoids last-minute scrambling.

lisa-peopleops: Proposed plan: 1) Ask Javier to upload the USCIS receipt + latest I-94 and any attorney contact info. 2) Postpone official paid start to Jun 22 for now. 3) Allow unpaid shadow sessions with manager approval only. 4) Draft clear inbound email about constraints. @omar-immigration can you confirm language we should use?

omar-immigration: Will send a short template for the offer/onboarding update. Also sharing a checklist for what we need below:

```
- Upload USCIS receipt notice (PDF)
- Upload most recent I-94
- Confirm whether STEM OPT or adjustment-based filing (C9 vs C17)
- Attorney contact (for verification)
- SSN application status (if applicable)
- Confirm preferred official start date (placeholder)
```

We'll include a sentence clarifying that no paid work may occur until authorization is in place and that remote shadowing is strictly non-productive.

javier-newhire: Thanks — I’ll upload the receipt + I-94 to the onboarding folder now and share my attorney contact. Appreciate the clarity. :thumbsup:

lisa-peopleops: Thanks everyone — I’ll draft the email update to Javier and post here for review before sending.

omar-immigration: Posted the template in #people-ops-pinned-docs and will drop it here in 20m.

maria-peopleops: Sounds good. I’ll hold benefits enrollment until we have confirmed first paid day.

(hr-bot automated): Note: This thread will be archived after 30 days unless marked for follow-up.
